narrative:

The most influential factor was your past class failures. You have none, which matches the average for students who passed, so this pushed the prediction toward passing. The second factor was your father’s education level. He completed primary school, which is less common among students who passed, and this pushed toward failing. The third factor was your reason for choosing this school. Choosing it because of home was the third strongest factor and pushed toward passing.

Your profile also shows strengths and areas to watch: you have zero absences, family support, and a wish to continue to higher education. However, you study less than two hours per week, while most students who passed study two to five hours or more. To improve, keep your attendance strong, protect your record of no failures, increase weekly study, use family support, and ask school staff about extra help and internet access for coursework. These steps can lower your remaining risk before the final year ends.
